3. BugMeNot has closed

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

The website BugMeNot, which provided shared login credentials for websites to bypass registration walls, has officially shut down. The service had operated for years as a tool for users to avoid creating accounts on various platforms.

My Take

BugMeNot was the digital equivalent of a communal key under the doormat, and frankly, I’m surprised it lasted this long in our era of hyper-paranoid authentication. We’ve traded the simplicity of shared passwords for a world where you need a biometric scan and a blood sacrifice just to read a recipe. Pour one out for the last bastion of internet laziness.

4. Optimizely compromised, served malware on Zoom, GitLab

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

Optimizely was compromised, leading to the distribution of malware through its platform to high-profile clients including Zoom and GitLab. The incident highlights the risks associated with third-party supply chain vulnerabilities in web services.

My Take

Nothing says 'we have top-tier security' like accidentally turning your customers' websites into malware delivery trucks. It’s a great reminder that your digital supply chain is only as secure as the weakest vendor you forgot you were using. Trusting third-party scripts is like letting a stranger hold your house keys because they promised to water the plants.

Summary
